text:
alex: Quick sync — I converted LlamaX-30B to safetensors and uploaded for onboarding. Need a couple quick sanity checks before I open the model entry + rollout.

jia: Thanks — where did you put the files? also how many shards and what's the TP layout?

alex: Path: s3://redwood-models/onboarding/llamax-30b/2026-03-10/
I uploaded 4 shards (tp_size=2 during conversion). Rough listing:

```
config.json
tokenizer.json
merges.txt
pytorch_model-00001-of-00004.safetensors
pytorch_model-00002-of-00004.safetensors
pytorch_model-00003-of-00004.safetensors
pytorch_model-00004-of-00004.safetensors
model-index.json
```

alex: Conversion notes: original ckpt in bf16, converted to float16 safetensors for smaller size. Used tensor-parallel layout: contiguous per TP rank (consecutive blocks), not interleaved.

sam: Do we have torch_dtype set in config/model-index? runtime validation flags missing dtype often.

alex: model-index.json includes:

```
{"format":"safetensors","shard_strategy":"tp_consecutive","tp_size":2,"torch_dtype":"float16"}
```

maria: Quick tokenizer note — tokenizer.json from the repo had eos_token_id: 50256 but our runtime expects eos=1 for the Llama family mapping. Also I saw bos token id mismatch (0 vs 1) in some tests. That will break streaming/truncation logic.

alex: Ugh — I saw that too. The original tokenizer was a hybrid repo tokenizer. I left tokenizer.json untouched. Suggest we normalize to our adapter mapping.

jia: Two quick checks I'll run:
- confirm shard ordering matches runtime expectation (tp_consecutive)
- run a small decode/encode roundtrip on tokenizer and compare special token ids

deploy-bot: model-validator: queued validation job 1765002475 for s3://redwood-models/onboarding/llamax-30b/2026-03-10/ — will run config + small sample generation.

sam: Float16 vs BF16 question: some attention ops in LlamaX were more stable in bf16 for long sequences. Did you run a short eval pass on 2k tokens?

alex: I ran a 256-token pass, seemed fine. I can run 2k before we flip to production — but keeping float16 for now to save memory. If we see perf regressions we'll keep a bf16 variant.

maria: For tokenizer fix I can patch tokenizer.json and push a normalized tokenizer into the same s3 path (tokenizer-normalized.json). Will also add a compatibility shim in model-index pointing at tokenizer-normalized.json.

alex: Great. Also note the sharding name pattern — runtime loader expects `pytorch_model-000XX-of-000YY.safetensors`, which we used, but verify the byte-order for embedding table shards (some converters accidentally reorder dims). Jia, can you checksum kv cache dims?

jia: On it. I'll run a quick shape check across shards (script: `python tools/verify_shards.py --path s3://...`). Will post results.

deploy-bot: model-validator: validation job 1765002475 completed — warnings: tokenizer.eos_id mismatch; config.torch_dtype= float16 OK; shard_count=4 OK; shard_shape_check: pending (deep check queued).

alex: Thanks. Maria/Jia, if you can push fixes today we can re-run validation and then I will file the model entry + quicknote in the console with recommended runtime options: {"tp_size":2, "preferred_dtype":"float16","allow_bf16_fallback":true, "tokenizer":"tokenizer-normalized.json"}.

maria: I'll update tokenizer and push patch by EOD. Will include a tiny README in the s3 folder explaining the token id mapping.

jia: Shape check looks good for linear layers, but embedding table kernel for shard 3 has dims swapped — small bug in the conversion script interleaving logic. I'll re-run conversion for that shard and upload replacement file: pytorch_model-00003-of-00004.safetensors

sam: Once replacement is up, remind me and I'll run a canary generate on Dedicated to observe latency/quality.

alex: Perfect. Ping me when both tokenizer and shard replacement are uploaded and I'll re-trigger the validator. :thumbsup:

maria: Will do. Thanks team.
